title: Where our food comes from
examples: Teacher, where does the flour for bread come from?
Can you show us where we get fish for dinner?
What is the difference between growing food and buying it?

explain.say: Today we are learning about where our food actually comes from.
Food from farms comes from growing plants and raising animals.
Fishing brings us food that comes from the ocean and rivers.
Some food items are processed in big factories near us.
Different seasons change what food is available to us.
Food miles measure the distance food travels to your plate.

faq.a: Food miles measure the total distance food has travelled from where it was grown or caught to the shop.
asks: How far did this food travel?
What does the distance of food mean?

faq.q: Are food miles always bad for the planet?
faq.a: Long food miles can mean more fuel was used for transport, which can create pollution.
asks: Is it bad to buy food from far away?

faq.q: Do all foods have food miles?
faq.a: Yes, almost all food has travelled some distance, even if it is just to the local shop.
asks: Does food travel even short distances?

faq.q: What is the best way to check food miles?
faq.a: Look for labels or ask at the shop where the food was grown or caught.
asks: How do I know the distance?
Where can I see the food's journey?

faq.q: Does the season change where we buy food?
faq.a: Yes, in certain seasons, local food is more plentiful and easier to find.
asks: Do we eat different things in winter?
Is there a best time to buy fruit?

facts: Farms provide crops like grains and vegetables for our meals.
Fishing supplies us with seafood from rivers and the sea.
Food factories process raw ingredients into items we buy.
Seasons change the types of food that are in season.
Food miles calculate the total travel distance of food.

quiz.say: If you buy apples grown on a farm nearby, what is the food mile distance likely to be?

options.show: A number based on the weather
options.say: A number based on the weather

quiz.why: Local food means it did not travel very far.

wrong.0: Food must travel at least to the shop.
wrong.1: Food miles are measured by distance, not weather.
wrong.3: This suggests the food came from a very distant place.

quiz.say: Which source provides food that is usually caught from water?
quiz.why: Fishing brings us seafood from the ocean and rivers.

wrong.0: Farms are for growing plants and raising animals on land.
wrong.1: Factories change food; they do not provide the raw food.
wrong.2: Food does not come from the sky.

quiz.say: If a food item travels from another country, what is the food mile distance likely to be?

options.show: A number based on the season
options.say: A number based on the season

quiz.why: International travel means the food has covered many miles.

wrong.1: A small number suggests it came from a nearby place.
wrong.2: It is impossible for food from another country to have zero miles.
wrong.3: Food miles measure distance, not the time of year.
